title: We are all Indians
source_note: NCERT structural and thematic alignment only. All teaching passages, checks, feedback, and assessment situations are original Zidd content.

levels.title: Read an Indian child's profile
levels.focus: match a child with a state, language, art, or interest
levels.teaching_goal: Read short original profiles and retrieve the correct detail without mixing information from two children.

guided_check.teaching_block: Profiles contain several details. Match the question word: where asks for a place; what language asks for a language name.
guided_check.passage: Aditi lives in Assam. She speaks Assamese with her grandparents and enjoys weaving paper mats.

bridge.teaching_block: Keep person, place, and activity together. A nearby place name from another profile would be a mix-up.
bridge.passage: Joel comes from Goa. He speaks Konkani and likes playing football near his school.

masterclass.teaching_block: Use the action clue. The state tells where; the hobby tells what the child enjoys doing.
masterclass.passage: Navya lives in Karnataka and speaks Kannada. On weekends, she learns to play the veena.
masterclass.prompt: What does Navya learn on weekends?

independent_check.teaching_block: Answer without choices. Return only the requested profile detail, not every fact.
independent_check.passage: Harnoor's family lives in Punjab. He speaks Punjabi and grows mint in a window pot.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer profile reading to an international pen-pal card. Match the question to the exact field.
transfer_check.passage: Maya lives in Nairobi, speaks Swahili and English, and enjoys making model planes.
transfer_check.prompt: Which hobby is listed on Maya's card?

levels.title: Find unity across differences
levels.focus: identify the main idea that people can differ and still belong together
levels.teaching_goal: Combine details about languages, homes, foods, and arts into the chapter's unity message.

guided_check.teaching_block: A main idea must include both difference and belonging. Do not choose one festival or language as the whole message.
guided_check.passage: Our class families speak six languages and cook many kinds of food. Everyone works together on the same school garden.
guided_check.prompt: Which statement gives the main idea?
options: People can be different and still work as one group.
Only one language belongs in school.
All families cook the same dish.
accepted_answers: People can be different and still work as one group.
people can be different and still work together
differences do not stop people belonging together

bridge.teaching_block: Unique means each person has special details. The shared identity does not erase those details.
bridge.passage: One child paints village scenes; another practises a hill dance. Both proudly call India their home.
options: Different traditions can belong to one country.
accepted_answers: Different traditions can belong to one country.
different traditions belong to one country
people with different traditions are all Indian

masterclass.teaching_block: Look beyond the list of objects. The repeated sharing shows respect and curiosity across differences.
masterclass.passage: Children bring a folk song, a family game, and a favourite story to culture day. They listen to every presentation.
masterclass.prompt: What is the paragraph mainly about?

independent_check.teaching_block: State the main idea in your own words. Include one difference and one way the group remains united.
independent_check.passage: The neighbours celebrate different festivals. When the lane floods, every family carries supplies to the same dry hall.
independent_check.prompt: What does this scene show about the neighbours?

concept_slots.description: Mention helping together during the flood.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer unity to a mixed-ability team. Show different strengths serving one shared goal.
transfer_check.passage: For a science model, Chen draws labels, Salma measures pieces, and Deep fixes the wheels. Their single model works well.
transfer_check.prompt: How are the teammates different yet united?

concept_slots.description: Mention the one working model or common goal.

levels.title: Use clues for culture words
levels.focus: understand language, festival, neighbour, monument, and unique
levels.teaching_goal: Infer cultural and community words from examples while keeping language names as names.

guided_check.teaching_block: A language is a system people use to speak, sign, read, or write with one another. Hindi and Tamil are examples, not describing words.
guided_check.passage: At home, Rohan speaks Hindi. His friend writes a note in Tamil. Both are using a language.
options: a way people communicate with words or signs
accepted_answers: a way people communicate with words or signs

bridge.teaching_block: A festival is a special time of celebration. Food and lights are clues, but one dish alone is not the meaning.
bridge.passage: The town holds a festival with songs, lamps, and a community meal.

masterclass.teaching_block: A neighbour is someone who lives close by. Friendship is possible, but living nearby is the key clue.
masterclass.passage: Mrs Das lives in the flat next to ours. She is our neighbour.
accepted_answers: a person who lives near us

independent_check.teaching_block: A monument is a special building or structure remembered for history. The age and visitor clues support the meaning.
independent_check.passage: The old stone monument has stood for hundreds of years, and visitors come to learn its history.
accepted_answers: a special historic building or structure

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer unique to a fingerprint activity. Different patterns show one of a kind, not better or worse.
transfer_check.passage: Every fingerprint card has a different pattern. Each print is unique.

levels.title: Separate names from describing words
levels.focus: recognise proper names, actions, and describing words in profile sentences
levels.teaching_goal: Treat names of people, places, and languages as naming words; identify adjectives only when they describe a noun.

guided_check.teaching_block: Marathi is the name of a language, so it is a proper naming word. Bright describes the shawl. Never classify Marathi as a describing word.
guided_check.passage: Vibha speaks Marathi and wears a bright shawl.

bridge.teaching_block: A place name is also a proper naming word. A describing word tells what kind, such as coastal.
bridge.passage: Luis visits coastal Goa during the holidays.

masterclass.teaching_block: An action word shows what someone does. Punjabi names a language; sings shows the action.
masterclass.passage: Gurleen sings in Punjabi at the school event.

independent_check.teaching_block: Classify by job in this fresh sentence. Kerala names a place even though it appears after a describing word.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer proper names to a world map. Spanish names a language; lively describes the music.
transfer_check.passage: Ana speaks Spanish and enjoys lively music.

levels.title: Join differences with but
levels.focus: use but to connect two different true details without making one seem wrong
levels.teaching_goal: Use but for a neutral contrast between preferences, abilities, or places, and because only for a reason.

guided_check.teaching_block: But can join different preferences. Both sides remain true; neither food is presented as better.
guided_check.passage: Ritu likes idli, ____ her brother prefers poha.

bridge.teaching_block: Use because only when the second part explains why. Here the second activity contrasts with the first.
bridge.passage: Zain plays the flute, ____ his friend dances.
bridge.prompt: Which word contrasts the two activities?

masterclass.teaching_block: A contrast can describe two languages without ranking them. Keep the names capitalised in the written sentence.
masterclass.passage: Mira speaks Bengali at home, ____ she uses English in science class.
masterclass.prompt: Which word joins the home and school language uses?

independent_check.teaching_block: Check whether the second idea is a cause. This sentence gives the reason everyone can join.
independent_check.passage: The game includes pictures ____ not everyone reads the same language.
independent_check.prompt: Which connector introduces the reason for using pictures?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer contrast to a family routine. Write one respectful sentence that uses but and keeps both choices equal.
transfer_check.passage: One cousin walks to the library. The other cousin cycles there.
transfer_check.prompt: Join the two travel choices in one sentence.

levels.title: Compare and welcome respectfully
levels.focus: write a short comparison or message that values both difference and belonging
levels.teaching_goal: Create concise comparisons and welcome messages that include accurate details and respectful common ground.

guided_check.teaching_block: A fair comparison states one difference and one shared point. It does not call either child strange.
guided_check.passage: Tashi enjoys thukpa, and Kavya enjoys dosa. Both love listening to stories.
options: They like different foods, but both enjoy stories.
Tashi's food is right and Kavya's is wrong.
accepted_answers: They like different foods, but both enjoy stories.
they like different foods but both enjoy stories
their foods differ but they both like stories

bridge.teaching_block: A welcome message names something the newcomer can share and shows interest without making guesses about the person's culture.
bridge.passage: A new student says she speaks Odia and likes badminton.
options: Welcome! Would you like to play badminton with us?
You must teach us every Odia word now.
accepted_answers: Welcome! Would you like to play badminton with us?
welcome would you like to play badminton with us
Welcome. Would you like to play badminton with us?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass check: include the different languages and the common activity in one clear sentence.
masterclass.passage: Rima speaks Nepali, and Ali speaks Urdu. Both enjoy chess club.
masterclass.prompt: How can we compare Rima and Ali?
accepted_answers: They speak different languages, but both enjoy chess club.
they speak different languages but both enjoy chess club
Rima speaks Nepali and Ali speaks Urdu, but both enjoy chess.
rima speaks nepali and ali speaks urdu but both enjoy chess

independent_check.teaching_block: Write a natural comparison. Include one accurate difference and one common point; exact wording is not required.
independent_check.passage: Nivedita paints clay pots. Farah makes paper flowers. Both decorate the school hall.
independent_check.prompt: Compare the two children in one or two sentences.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer respectful welcome to a sports camp with children from different countries. Include greeting and common ground.
transfer_check.passage: A camper from Bhutan joins Leena's team and says he loves table tennis. Leena loves the game too.
transfer_check.prompt: Write a short welcome Leena could give.

concept_slots.description: Mention their shared interest in table tennis.

items.passage: Pari lives in Himachal Pradesh, speaks Hindi, and enjoys growing beans.
Biren comes from Sikkim. He speaks Nepali and likes sketching mountain birds.
Fathima lives in Kerala and reads Malayalam stories to her little brother.
Ritwik lives in West Bengal. He speaks Bengali and collects fallen leaves for art.
At lunch, children open boxes with many different dishes. They trade recipes and eat at one table.
items.prompt: Which statement captures the lunch-table scene?
options: Different food traditions can be shared with friendship.
Everyone must eat the same dish.
accepted_answers: Different food traditions can be shared with friendship.
different foods can be shared with friendship
different traditions can bring friends together

items.passage: The choir sings verses in three languages. All singers join the same chorus.
items.prompt: What larger idea does the multilingual chorus show?
options: Different languages can be part of one performance.
A choir should use only one voice.
accepted_answers: Different languages can be part of one performance.
different languages can belong in one song
many languages can unite in one performance

items.passage: Families wear different styles of dress at the school fair. Everyone helps serve water to visitors.
items.prompt: Explain how the families are different yet united.

items.passage: Some children travel by bus and some walk. They all arrive to plant trees in the same park.
Our neighbour lives across the landing and waters our plant when we travel.
items.prompt: Which choice tells who a neighbour is?

items.passage: The harvest festival includes dancing, a special meal, and decorated carts.
items.prompt: What do these details show a festival is?

items.passage: The fort is a monument visited by people who want to learn about the city's past.
No two rangoli cards have the same pattern; every design is unique.
items.prompt: How are the card patterns described?

items.passage: Suhana speaks Marathi and carries a heavy drum.
items.prompt: Identify the proper name of the language.

items.passage: The lively dancer performs in Jaipur.
Anand reads Telugu beside the open window.
The bright boat crosses the lake.
Aman enjoys chess, ____ Zara prefers carrom.
The welcome card uses pictures ____ the new child is still learning English.
Jaya speaks Kannada at home, ____ she reads English books at school.
We ask politely ____ a new word may need explanation.
Lalita makes a bamboo basket. Yusuf paints a cloth bag. Both bring their work to craft day.
options: They make different crafts, but both share their work.
They do exactly the same task.
accepted_answers: They make different crafts, but both share their work.
they make different crafts but both share their work

items.passage: A new student says he speaks Tamil and enjoys cricket.
options: Welcome! We can play cricket together.
accepted_answers: Welcome! We can play cricket together.
welcome we can play cricket together
Welcome. We can play cricket together.

items.passage: Mansi learns Bharatanatyam. Dorjee practises a mask dance. Both perform at the school event.
A new neighbour from Nagaland joins the lane's reading circle and says she likes adventure stories.
items.prompt: Write a short welcome from the group.

concept_slots.description: Mention reading or adventure stories together.
